brief: Weekend desk note from Goldman's Quek. Two risks that lingered for months, geopolitical re-escalation and rising yields, compounded into one move after Jackson Hole and a US-Iran oil spike, so the desk reads volatility as dormant rather than dead. Post CPI it now expects a 25bp Fed hike in September, attributing that call to reluctance to surprise a market pricing near 90% odds rather than to the economy, while still reading the 2% inflation overshoot as fading one-time factors. It adds a 25bp ECB hike in December, pushes ECB normalization back two quarters to 4Q27, keeps the BOJ hiking next Friday, and lifts Brent forecasts by $5 to $85 by year end. History says US equities struggle for three months after hikes then return +9% over twelve, so earnings delivery is the swing factor: results and balance sheets are robust, Asia is priced on 34% earnings CAGR through 2028, and a $30/bbl oil rise costs only 4%. GS Prime bought global TMT the most in seven months and sold Financials. Conference tone was decisively positive on AI demand versus tight supply, with Power the least appreciated bottleneck and its basket positioning in the 4th percentile.
